answer: Shared Cost Ledger: each identity's actions carry a maintenance charge debited from a single payment account, and the ledger shares that account's history across all identities it funds. An agent seeking to forge many clones must pay the accumulated charge for every identity linked to that account, so cloning multiplies fixed costs rather than spreading them thin. A whisper of collusion shows up as one account bearing many charges, raising its per-identity expense above honest operation. Cheap capacity on a single terrace of accounts gets priced out,
